items.excerpt: A report claims SpaceX is internally testing a handheld AI device that would offer a dedicated hardware gateway to xAI's Grok models — Elon Musk publicly called the report 'utterly false', but the rumor adds to the wave of big AI players exploring first-party gadgets.

Project Mirage unveiled Dune, a 50-gram three-button MacBook keypad whose keys change function based on the app in use, offering context-aware shortcuts and AI-powered automation for meetings and productivity apps.

The Dune keypad attaches three 'smart' AI macro buttons to a MacBook Air or Pro; their function adapts to the app currently in use, marketed as an aluminum 50-gram AI upgrade for Apple laptops. (Same product as the Digital Trends item — alternate outlet.)
With watchOS 27 beta 3, Apple switched on Siri AI and a dedicated Siri app on Apple Watch, bringing the LLM-powered assistant to the wrist for the first time.

Apple says the Home app's new Apple Intelligence camera features in iOS 27 — AI-generated summaries and search of smart-home camera footage — will require an iCloud+ plan starting at 2TB, putting a paywall on home-camera AI.

Code in iOS 27 beta 2 references an unreleased Apple product that points to camera-equipped AirPods Pro — hardware that would give Apple Intelligence's Visual Intelligence features eyes on the world from your ears.

Apple's latest betas add a disclosure popup for AI features whose processing leaves the device for Google Cloud servers — a notable transparency shift at the on-device/off-device boundary of Siri AI and Apple Intelligence.
With the Gemini-first Google Home Speaker now out, 9to5Google maps what a next-gen 'Google Home Display' smart display should be — the hardware gap in Google's Gemini smart-home lineup.
Scientists developed a color-changing tactile sensor that lets robots visualize touch in real time — a step toward more precise robotic manipulation, prosthetics, and surgery.
Chinese robotics company Agibot lays out its consumer humanoid roadmap: robots taking over 'dangerous' jobs first, with home companions that could one day even teach children.
Weave Robotics' Isaac 1 is a $7,999 legless home robot on a stalk that folds laundry and handles basic chores — a pragmatic counterpoint to the humanoid home-robot hype.
Samsung is developing a fingernail-sized storage chip to replace M.2 SSDs in thin devices, promising better battery life and faster on-device AI inference in future laptops and AI PCs.
Google is prepping a toggle for Gemini Live's 'guided vision' mode, which highlights objects through your phone's camera — giving users finer control over how the assistant sees the world.
Gemini Live is working on an optional push-to-talk input mode so the assistant only listens while you hold a button instead of listening constantly — a privacy-minded shift in device voice UX.
First-generation Amazon Echo speakers are reportedly failing en masse — slow or no responses — highlighting the lifecycle cliff for aging smart speakers left behind by the Alexa+ generative-AI era.

MSI's Claw 8 EX AI+ is the first device built on Intel's dedicated handheld SoC (Arc G3 Extreme CPU + Arc B390 iGPU), and Notebookcheck's review verdict crowns the AI-branded handheld the fastest in its class.
Gizmodo reviews the Aqara Camera Hub G350, an indoor Matter smart camera hub with on-board detection smarts — excellent for the AI smart home, if slightly creepy with its bunny ears.

Ahead of Samsung's July 22 Unpacked, a leak details the Galaxy Watch 9 and Watch Ultra 2: a new Snapdragon chip to power more on-watch AI, plus new health features, watch faces, and a revamped companion app.
